title: Streaming consumer patterns and robust retry semantics for Python chat streams
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: SDK users building streaming chat experiences currently choose between two awkward options: an event/callback API that is cheap and low-overhead but difficult to compose with async code, or an async-iterator API that composes well but requires buffering and can be surprising under backpressure. Both surface awkward retry semantics when network or runtime errors interrupt a partial stream (how do we resume without duplicating assistant tokens or losing user context?).

Goal: Provide a first-class, ergonomically consistent Python SDK surface that: 1) supports event-first callbacks for low-latency handlers, 2) exposes an async iterator for for-await workflows, and 3) provides clear retry / resume semantics for interrupted streams with practical trade-offs documented. The implementation must be lightweight (minimal per-message allocation), support cancellation, and be compatible with existing runtime resume tokens where available.

Design summary: implement a small adapter layer (StreamConsumer) that can be instantiated in one of three modes: callback, iterator, or hybrid. Core pieces:
- StreamEvent (type tag strings): delta (partial assistant tokens), role_change, done, error, heartbeat
- Event bus: a single-producer, multi-consumer asyncio.Queue with configurable maxsize and an internal token-count semaphore to enforce read-ahead budget (prevents unbounded memory growth).
- Adapter: exposes subscribe(callback) which returns an unsubscribe handle; and async_iter() which returns an async generator. Both consume from the same queue so handlers can coexist.
- Backpressure: runtime read-ahead limited by queue maxsize; when full the adapter signals the transport layer (via awaitable backpressure API) to pause consumption. We will add a best-effort path to emit a small credit increase to allow low-latency handlers to process without immediate bulk buffering.
- Retry / resume semantics: primary approach is optimistic resume using runtime-provided resume_token when available. If resume_token absent, fall back to idempotent-retry rules: for requests marked idempotent (client-provided idempotency_key), we attempt server-side resume; otherwise we surface a RetryRequired error and provide helpers to: 1) restart stream and dedupe assistant fragments client-side by comparing content checksums, or 2) reconstruct assistant output by including prior stable messages as system context (documented trade-off: higher token cost).
- Cancellation and partial-consumption: cancel() will drain the transport but will not drop already-delivered events; unsubscribes stop further deliveries.

Implementation notes: aim for <= 150 lines of core adapter logic. Keep internal representation simple (tuples or small namedtuple) to avoid heavy allocations. Provide two public helper utilities: stream_to_text(stream) which reconstructs stable assistant text from deltas, and safe_retry_restart(request, last_stable_sentences).

Compatibility: ensure parity with TypeScript/Go SDKs by matching event shape and semantics (documented in shared spec). Add migration guide for users currently using on_message callbacks or consuming raw bytes.
acceptance_criteria: Public API: StreamConsumer.subscribe(callback) + StreamConsumer.async_iter() are documented and stable
Adapter handles simultaneous callback and iterator consumers without duplicating events
Backpressure enforced end-to-end: runtime read-ahead capped and queue maxsize prevents OOM in long-running streams
Retry/resume behavior documented with tests covering resume_token present and absent cases
Integration tests with runtime mock exercising partial-delta streams, cancellations, and resumed streams
API review sign-off from SDK PM and runtime owner
Example notebook and short snippet in SDK README demonstrating callback -> iterator adapter and safe_retry_restart helper
comments: 2026-03-02 - Triage: flagged as priority after customer support ticket where an interrupted stream duplicated assistant output for a chat widget (internal ref: INC-4421). Aisha assigned to write initial spec.

2026-03-05 - Design review: discussed event taxonomy and decided to include explicit 'heartbeat' events to make idle detection reliable for mobile clients. Agreed to use queue + semaphore for backpressure rather than per-message ACKs to avoid complexity.

2026-03-08 - Spike complete: prototype implemented in branch feat/stream-adapter-py (github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/pull/412). Basic adapter + iterator works; found a race when unsubscribe occurs during resume flow (investigating).
2026-03-10 - PM review: requested clearer examples for non-idempotent restart flow and a library helper to compute simple content checksums for dedupe. Added safe_retry_restart helper to spec.

2026-03-12 - Runtime sync: runtime team confirmed resume_token semantics for dedicated and hosted are available but may not be present for all legacy models; agreed on a fallback path. Added ENG-17110 to track runtime changes needed for deterministic resume tokens.

2026-03-14 - Engineering update: found a subtle deadlock when queue maxsize == 1 combined with long-running callback handlers; mitigation: adapter will run callbacks in a background Task group with bounded concurrency. This is blocking for final API doc example (investigating perf impact).
